_about: Open clinical questions for the oncologist's sign-off of this case's rubric (shown in scripts/build_case_review.py). Each comes from the structured decision-rule authoring pass on 2026-10-23.

questions.question: Is Pola-R-CHP "R-CHOP-based" for this dangerous curative-regimen item? It's currently counted as yes, which keeps a Pola-R-CHP answer from being flagged dangerous for this low-risk, IPI 0 patient.
options: Pola-R-CHP should not count (it's an escalation, not standard-of-care here)

questions.question: With the structured rule, a DA-EPOCH-R or R-CHOEP order now fails the dangerous curative-regimen item AND costs 5 points from the separate over-intensification item. Is that double penalty intended for this IPI 0, low-risk patient, or should it only cost the one item?
options: Should only cost the mn_da_epoch points

questions.question: Should this item mean exactly 6 cycles of an R-CHOP-based or Pola-R-CHP regimen, or 6 or more? It's currently encoded as 6 or more.

The over-staging item's text only lists stage III or IV as the error, so overstaging to stage II currently only loses the stage_i points (7), not a dangerous flag. Should overstaging to stage II also be dangerous for this stage I patient?
options: Stage II should also be dangerous

questions.question: Is condoms/barrier method alone acceptable as "effective non-estrogen contraception" during treatment? The existing prose rule accepts it, so the new structured rule does too.
questions.context: Barrier methods have a materially higher real-world failure rate than LARC options.
options: Require a more effective non-estrogen method (IUD/implant/progestin-only pill)

questions.question: For the FLYER regimen (4 x R-CHOP + 2 x rituximab-only doses), should the structured "cycles" field be recorded as 4 (chemo cycles) or 6 (counting the rituximab-only doses)? Both are currently accepted when the regimen string itself says 4 x R-CHOP, but this should be stated explicitly in the answer-authoring instruction to avoid models guessing.
